strings: Soothing Turtle Bisque is a culinary task offered by Christoph Jeffcoat in Tarren Mill. The Forsaken cook aims to disprove the notion that the undead lack culinary talent by preparing a hearty broth from local snapjaw meat. Players must hunt freshwater turtles around the waterways of Hillsbrad Foothills and the shores of Lordamere Lake to master his prized recipe.

It is widely assumed that the Forsaken have entirely abandoned the comforts of life, including the art of fine dining. Christoph Jeffcoat, stationed in Tarren Mill, vigorously rejects that assumption. Boasting that his rich, soothing turtle bisque is good enough to tempt souls back from beyond the grave, Jeffcoat seeks to prove that undead hands are capable of delicate, heartwarming craft even in a land tainted by plague and war.

Ordinarily, Jeffcoat gathered his own ingredients from the waterways of Hillsbrad Foothills and the eastern shores of Lordamere Lake in neighboring Alterac. However, duties in Tarren Mill and the encroaching presence of Alliance forces have pinned him down. He relies on passing Horde cooks to hunt the snapjaws, harvest their meat, and bring it back so the culinary tradition can endure.
Why does a Forsaken cook care about making hot bisque?

While the Forsaken do not require sustenance in the same manner as living mortals, individuals like Christoph Jeffcoat take great pride in their trade. Jeffcoat aims to disprove the prejudice that undead lack refined skill, joking that his signature broth is good enough to bring the deceased back to life.

Tarren Mill serves as the primary Horde stronghold in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Formerly a human village, it now functions as a fortified base for the Forsaken and their allies, facing frequent clashes against Southshore and the regional Alliance presence.

This task allows cooks to master Soothing Turtle Bisque, turning the aggressive reptiles of Lordamere Lake and Hillsbrad's rivers into a restorative meal.
Christoph Jeffcoat represents a lighter, craft-driven side of the Forsaken, insisting that death has not dulled his culinary passion.

This step in the investigation leads deep into an old crate of Flintridge heirlooms left beside the canals of Stormwind City. Sifting through the dusty relics uncovers a torn journal page, offering a vital handwritten clue to the past life of Stalvan Mistmantle that leads to Marshal Haggard in Elwynn Forest.

While digging through a sealed crate filled with musty heirlooms, old hunting trophies, and family portraits, investigators uncover a lone torn journal page hidden beneath a ceramic vase. Written in Stalvan Mistmantle's own hand, this remnant provides an intimate glimpse into the mind of a reclusive scholar before tragedy struck.

Marshal Haggard, now aged and plagued by failing eyesight, struggles to read the script on the battered parchment. Even so, the distinctive handwriting strikes an uneasy chord in his memory, recalling documents and incidents from years past before the darkness took his sight.
Where is the sealed crate located?

The sealed crate sits by the Canals of Stormwind City, directly behind Caretaker Folsom among the Flintridge family's packed-up belongings. The page you find there is then taken to Marshal Haggard in southeastern Elwynn Forest.

This errand delivers a strange petrified specimen recovered from the wild beaches of Darkshore to the Explorers' League outpost in Darnassus. Archaeologist Hollee refuses to abandon her distracted colleague in the field, entrusting the specimen's transport to a passing adventurer instead. The fossil's arrival in the night elven capital immediately captures the keen interest of Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker.

Prospector Remtravel's excavations along the misty coast of Darkshore have unearthed a curious fossil, but digging deeper matters more to him than protocol. Archaeologist Hollee, unwilling to leave the wandering prospector alone amidst the shore's dangerous beasts and hostile cultists, remains behind to watch over him. In order to get the discovery documented, she requires an Alliance traveler to ferry the specimen up to Darnassus, where the dwarven guild maintains a scholarly delegation.

Dwarves from Ironforge have crossed the Great Sea in force under the banner of the Explorers' League, eager to unearth ancient relics and lost history beneath the soil of Kalimdor. Receiving the artifact in the elven capital, Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker wastes no time in marveling over Remtravel's knack for uncovering ancient treasures. While night elves view their forests as living sanctuaries, the League views the ancient lands as an expansive archaeological dig waiting to be deciphered.

It is an unidentified petrified specimen unearthed along the coast of Darkshore by Prospector Remtravel. Its antiquity and strange nature make it a prize finding for the Explorers' League scholars stationed in Darnassus.

Watching dwarven excavators bring ancient remnants out of Darkshore's sacred soil can be jarring, but cooperating with the League preserves Alliance bonds.

The Ashenvale Hunt is a summons dispatched to young Horde champions visiting Thunder Bluff, urging them north into the dense canopy of Ashenvale. Delivered by the city's heralds, the call directs travelers to report to Senani Thunderheart at Splintertree Post to take part in a proving hunt.
A Summons from the High Rise

Within the serene heights of Thunder Bluff, runners keep the burgeoning Horde informed of opportunities beyond the borders of Mulgore. Bluff Runner Windstrider carries an open invitation aimed at proven adventurers looking for greater challenges. With the Horde establishing footholds deep in the ancient forest north of the Barrens, young warriors are called upon to bolster those outposts and test their survival skills in a far harsher environment.

Ashenvale represents both rich resources and severe peril for the Horde. Two prominent encampments anchor the faction's presence in the territory: Splintertree Post along the main road, and a remote outpost perched upon the western coast at Zoram Strand. Arriving at Splintertree Post puts incoming recruits directly under the wing of Senani Thunderheart, a veteran outdoorswoman organizing a massive hunt designed to tame the wilderness and claim glory for the Horde.

Bluff Runner Windstrider offers this assignment to passing adventurers in Thunder Bluff. His duty is to alert capable fighters to the Horde's expansion efforts and point them toward remote outposts in need of aid.

Dangers of the Windfury is a rite of martial readiness offered by Ruul Eagletalon in Bloodhoof Village. Young tauren and Horde adventurers are tasked with battling the savage Windfury harpies nesting in the southeastern cliffs of Mulgore. Hunting these feral predators serves as an essential test of skill and survival before journeying beyond the tribal homeland.

In Bloodhoof Village, the veteran warrior Ruul Eagletalon observes all travelers who pass through the heart of Mulgore. For those coming of age or seeking to prove themselves ready for wider adventures, Ruul demands tangible proof of their combat instincts. Survival beyond the sheltered valleys of Mulgore requires poise against aggressive, cunning foes, and Ruul uses the land's fiercest native predators to measure a youth's mettle.

The Windfury harpies roost along the mountainous southeastern rim of Mulgore, safely off the beaten trails but constantly posing a threat to wandering wildlife and isolated travelers. Vicious and relentlessly hungry for fresh flesh, these avian terrors rely on swift swoops and razor-sharp claws. Defeating them and claiming their talons demonstrates not only the power to defeat an entrenched threat, but the speed required to counter aerial raiders.

Ruul Eagletalon is an experienced tauren warrior and teacher residing in Bloodhoof Village. He mentors young adventurers, offering trials to ensure they possess the strength, reflexes, and fortitude needed before setting out into the wider, more perilous corners of Kalimdor.

For young tauren, clearing Windfury nests is both an act of defending the plains and a sacred passage into acknowledged adulthood under the watchful eyes of village elders.

Assigned by Baine Bloodhoof in Bloodhoof Village, this task sends young Horde adventurers to curb the destructive poaching of the local Palemane gnolls. By culling their tanners, skinners, and poachers, you protect Mulgore's wildlife and learn the tauren philosophy of living in balance with the Earth Mother.

The tauren hold deep reverence for the natural world, taking from it only what is necessary to survive and honoring the Earth Mother in all things. The Palemane gnolls, having settled south of Bloodhoof Village and in a cavern to the west, harbor no such respect. Rather than hunting in moderation, they aggressively butcher wildlife across the plains, leaving stripped carcasses and upset ecosystems in their wake. For a people striving to build a peaceful homeland in Mulgore, this reckless slaughter cannot be tolerated.

Baine Bloodhoof initially hoped to resolve the matter peacefully, attempting to open dialogue with the encroaching gnolls. The Palemanes rejected every overture, answering diplomacy with hostility and continued devastation. Seeing that negotiation is futile, Baine turns to force. Young braves are sent directly to their hunting camps to put down the poachers, tanners, and skinners before the grasslands suffer permanent damage.
The Circle of Life and Death

This mission serves as a rite of passage and a moral lesson for growing champions. Upon returning from the culling, Baine reminds the adventurer that taking life must never be done out of malice, but out of necessity to maintain harmony. Life and death exist as an interconnected circle where one cannot thrive without the other, a foundational truth every guardian of Mulgore must carry forward.
Baine Bloodhoof, son of High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof, offers this task in Bloodhoof Village in central Mulgore.

For young tauren, answering Baine's call is an essential step in learning the sacred duty of defending Mulgore and honoring the Earth Mother's balance.

Dwarven Digging is a quest in Mulgore given by Baine Bloodhoof in Bloodhoof Village. Concerned that dwarven excavations will enrage the native beasts and defile the sacred earth, Baine tasks young Horde defenders with sabotaging their efforts by confiscating and shattering their pickaxes.

Northwest of Bloodhoof Village, dwarven prospectors have begun staking out a dig site in the rolling hills of Mulgore. The Explorer's League and its excavation crews seek titan relics and earthen secrets across Kalimdor, but their operations rarely respect indigenous lands or customs. To the tauren, the earth is a living mother to be revered, not stripped and hollowed for stones and metal.

Baine Bloodhoof recognizes that the dwarven machinery and relentless blasting threaten the fragile harmony of the plains. Beyond the physical destruction, the commotion agitates the local wildlife, stirring the plains kodos into frenzy. By smashing the prospectors' tools at their own forges, the tauren hope to send a blunt message and stall the encroachment before lasting harm is done.

Dwarven prospectors believe hidden secrets and artifacts lie deep within the earth of central Kalimdor. However, their disregard for tribal territory and violent mining methods have brought them into direct conflict with the tauren.

The Earth Mother's body is sacred, and seeing foreign intruders bore into Mulgore's rolling steppes is an affront that demands an immediate, firm response.

The Hunt Begins is a foundational rite of passage for young adventurers in Camp Narache on Red Cloud Mesa. Tasked by Grull Hawkwind, initiates are sent to hunt local plainstriders to provide meat and feathers for the village. Fulfilling this task marks the first step toward earning the respect of Chief Hawkwind and eventually gaining entry into Thunder Bluff.

On the heights of Red Cloud Mesa, survival and tradition intertwine. The tauren hunt out of necessity to feed and clothe their people, while also viewing the stalk and chase as a vital test of discipline and sport. When the stores of Camp Narache run lean, the community looks to its rising youth to gather fresh plainstrider meat for cooking and sturdy feathers for tribal garments.

No aspiring hero simply walks off Red Cloud Mesa into the wider reaches of Mulgore without proving their worth. Grull Hawkwind serves as a primary judge of character for the newcomers, insisting that one must prove their capability before stepping before his father, Chief Hawkwind. Bringing in a clean hunt demonstrates not only self-reliance, but devotion to supporting the tribe.
Grull Hawkwind offers this task in Camp Narache. He is the son of the village leader, Chief Hawkwind, and acts as an early mentor to young hunters and adventurers on Red Cloud Mesa.

Poison Water begins the tauren effort to purge pollution from Mulgore's sacred wells. Entrusted by Mull Thunderhorn in Bloodhoof Village, young Horde defenders gather natural components from the plains to craft a restorative ritual totem.

The grassy plains of Mulgore are sacred ground to the tauren, but insidious forces have begun threatening their vital lifeblood. Mull Thunderhorn, an elder stationed in Bloodhoof Village, discovers that goblin interlopers and their lackeys have tainted the precious water wells that sustain the tribes and the local wildlife. The pollution strikes directly at the spiritual heart of the nomadic people who recently settled here.

To counteract industrial contaminants, Mull relies on traditional tauren shamanism rather than crude remedies. Cleansing the Winterhoof Water Well requires crafting a potent ritual totem imbued with the vitality of Mulgore's indigenous predators. He sends hunters to track prairie wolves for their paws and mature plainstriders for their talons across the southwestern plains, enlisting the strength of the land to heal its own wounds.

Goblin encroachers and their hirelings are responsible for fouling the sacred watering holes across Mulgore. Their destructive industrial operations and disregard for natural balance threaten both the tauren tribes and local wildlife.

The desecration of fresh water strikes at the core of the Earth Mother's gifts, making the cleansing ritual a fundamental duty for any tauren coming of age in Mulgore.

Morin Cloudstalker directs travelers to examine the wreckage of an ambushed Venture Company caravan near the northern shore of Stonebull Lake. Although the tauren torched the convoy in retribution for lost comrades, goblin salvagers returned to recover intact cargo. Investigating the surviving supply crates reveals the true industrial scale of the Venture Company's operations in Mulgore.

The charred remnants along the northern bank of Stonebull Lake are the result of a swift strike by the tauren. Grieving the loss of two companions killed in an earlier skirmish, Morin Cloudstalker and his warriors ambushed an armed Venture Company supply convoy. Intending to obliterate the intruders' efforts, the tauren torched the wagons and abandoned the smoking ruin, presuming fire would consume whatever the goblins sought to haul.

The tauren soon noticed Venture Company salvagers scouring the blackened debris, suggesting their fire had failed to destroy the most crucial cargo. Rather than risk further lives blindly, Morin dispatches scouts to inspect the wreckage. Among the soot-stained wreckage rest intact crates marked with the insignia of the Venture Company Mining Division, packed and destined for central processing facilities.
Morin Cloudstalker and his tauren warriors ambushed and torched the caravan in retaliation after losing two of their scouts in a previous clash with the Venture Company.
